title: The World Bank recalibrated its global poverty line in 2025
body: The international extreme poverty line changed from 2.15 to 3 international dollars per person per day in June 2025. The update uses a newer set of price comparisons between economies.
takeaway: A change in the poverty estimate can come from how prices are measured as well as from how much people earn.
source: World Bank, June 2025 Update to Global Poverty Lines

title: An inflation index can account for shoppers switching products
body: In the US chained Consumer Price Index, spending patterns help determine how much each group of goods contributes. If shoppers buy less of a product after it becomes dearer, this affects the basket used in the comparison.
takeaway: A fixed basket answers what yesterday's choices would cost, while a changing basket can reflect new choices.
source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Chained Consumer Price Index FAQ

title: The US central bank has an employment goal as well as a price goal
body: The 1977 amendment to the Federal Reserve Act directs the US central bank to promote maximum employment, stable prices and moderate long-term interest rates. The first two goals are commonly called the dual mandate.
takeaway: Policy can face a trade-off when measures aimed at one goal make the other harder to reach in the short run.
source: U.S. Federal Reserve, Remarks on the Dual Mandate (2024)
